assertions.name: no_convention_member_reaches_B_over_A_plateau_AT_THE_m_e_SCALE
assertions.source: max over the family is 1.4156404 MeV/nucleon AT m_e; the empirical B/A plateau is 8.5 MeV/nucleon (independent: nuclear data). ⚠ The scale qualifier is not cosmetic: at the corpus's own E_0 the same family gives 11.596588 MeV/nucleon at its maximum and every member CLEARS the plateau, which is why this probe's verdict is withdrawn.

description: A1/qou-78pt: measures the span of the Markov-normalisation convention family against the extensive-term deficit. The family is discrete and 1.33x wide. VERDICT WITHDRAWN 2026-08-31: the 6-15x deficit was an m_e-vs-E_0 energy-scale artifact; at E_0 the deficit is 1.36-1.81x, the same size as the span, so A1 reverts to unfalsifiable-as-written. See the SCALE_CORRECTION data block.

span.verdict: span (1.33x) is two orders of magnitude smaller than the deficit (6-15x)

SCALE_CORRECTION_2026_08_31_VERDICT_WITH.what_is_wrong: Every MeV figure here uses m_e as the energy scale, unjustified. The corpus's binding machinery uses E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)).
SCALE_CORRECTION_2026_08_31_VERDICT_WITH.why_the_verdict_falls: The refutation was 'span 1.33x vs deficit 6-15x, two orders of magnitude too small'. Corrected, the deficit against a_V is 1.36-1.81x and the span is 1.33x -- the SAME SIZE. That is precisely the condition under which picking a member is a fit, i.e. the ROAST's original charge. A1 REVERTS to 'unfalsifiable as written'; pinning the convention from the axioms is again the actual work.

unreconciled_RESOLVED_2026_08_31.resolution: E_0-scaled, not m_e-scaled. 2.91/E_0 = 0.69517749, which is ln 2 = 0.69314718 to 0.3% -- the ROAST's own stated construction 'the extensive coefficient is E_0 log N' at N = 2. At m_e the figure is UNREACHABLE: it would need a normaliser with log = 5.69473, against a family whose logs span 0.694-0.923. Failing to reproduce it was the tell; I logged it as open instead of chasing it.

unreconciled_ORIGINAL_TEXT_kept_for_the_.note: 6-8x apart; the ROAST does not show its construction and this probe does not reconstruct it. The span argument is a ratio and is unaffected either way.

data.verdict: [WITHDRAWN 2026-08-31 -- see SCALE_CORRECTION block. Kept verbatim so the retraction has something to point at.] A1 REFUTED, not unfitted. The ROAST called the option unfalsifiable because 'do not normalise' is a convention family and choosing the member that lands on a_V would be a fit. Measured, the family is DISCRETE (the two leading members differ by exactly one factor of q) and spans 1.33x, while the deficit is 6-15x. No member lands on a_V, so there is no fit available -- the option fails uniformly over the family. Pinning the convention from the axioms, which the ROAST called 'the actual work', is therefore not needed to dispose of A1.
